All data, people and systems are fictional (Kalmia Coffee Roasters Inc.); nothing is scanned or tested in this lab.

1Install Python and check the version[1][2]

  1. Download Python 3.15 from python.org/downloads (any version 3.10 or newer works).
  2. Windows, 64-bit installer: tick Add python.exe to PATH, then Install Now. PATH is the list of folders where Windows looks for programs.
  3. Open a terminal — a window where you type commands — and type python --version (macOS and Linux: python3 --version).
Check: The terminal answers Python 3.15.0 or another version from 3.10 up.

2Put the starter pack in one folder[3]

  1. From the lecture module (section All tonight's files), download the workbook, kalmia_seed_scenarios.csv, kalmia_risk_register.py, kalmia_prioritizer.html, ir_readiness.csv, ir_timeline.csv and priority_list.csv.
  2. Create a folder such as Documents/420-1C2/Lab3 and move the seven files into it.
  3. Check each download link on VirusTotal before clicking (Legal Notice, section 14 and Annex C).
Check: One folder holds seven files; nothing else is needed.

3Score the readiness capabilities C1 to C8[4]

  1. Sheet Readiness: give each capability a score from 0 to 3 and write one piece of evidence (KRF [Kalmia risk factor], U, INC or an interview).
  2. A 3 needs a test record from the last 12 months (restore log, exercise report).
  3. Then give every scenario its response readiness: LOW by default, MODERATE when a scenario-specific response has worked, HIGH only when it is documented, approved and tested.
Check: Kalmia today: 5 / 24 = 20.8 % → LOW (change a score only with new evidence).

4Complete and extend the register[4]

  1. Sheet Register: verify the twelve seed rows, then add rows R-13 and up until the register holds 20 rows or more.
  2. Scenario = one sentence of 12 words or more: threat source, threat event, risk factor, asset, consequence.
  3. Fill likelihood and impact with their justifications, readiness, owner (Nadia Roy, Karim Haddad or Sophie Tremblay), status and review date (YYYY-MM-DD).
  4. Never type the score or the level: grey cells are formulas.
Check: Every row is complete; score and level appear by themselves.

5Read the heat map[5]

  1. Sheet Matrix: your identifiers appear in the 25 cells automatically.
  2. Write 3 to 5 sentences for the memo: risks per band, where the CRITICAL and HIGH risks sit, whether impact or frequency drives them, one case of range compression.
Check: The counts per level add up to the number of rows in your register.

6Prioritize: classes, escalation, keys, deadlines[6]

  1. Base class: CRITICAL → P1, HIGH → P2, MEDIUM → P3, LOW → P4.
  2. Escalation: a HIGH risk with a score of 15 or more, active threat evidence and LOW readiness becomes P1.
  3. Inside a class: score → impact → criticality → threat evidence → readiness (LOW first) → identifier.
  4. Open kalmia_prioritizer.html, click Load my CSV, choose your CSV (comma-separated values) export of step 8, then click Download CSV.
Check: The prioritizer ranking and the Ranking sheet are identical; deadlines are 2026-11-21 (P1), 2026-12-14 (P2), 2027-02-12 (P3) and 2027-11-14 (P4).

7Compute the ALE of the three to five highest risks

  1. Sheet ALE (annualized loss expectancy): SLE (single loss expectancy) = AV (asset value) × EF (exposure factor); ALE = SLE × ARO (annualized rate of occurrence) (Class 10 method).
  2. Give the source of each value (interview, invoice, incident record).
  3. R-01: $250,000 × 0.60 = $150,000 per event; × 0.5 per year = $75,000 per year.
Check: Each top risk has an ALE (annualized loss expectancy) with its sources.

8Export the Register sheet as CSV[7]

  1. Click the Register tab, then save it as CSV (comma-separated values) named Lab3_register.csv.
  2. Excel: File → Save As → CSV UTF-8 (Comma delimited). LibreOffice: File → Save a Copy → Text CSV, character set UTF-8 (Unicode Transformation Format, 8-bit — the text encoding that keeps accented letters such as é).
  3. Keep the workbook itself as .xlsx: the CSV (comma-separated values) holds only the active sheet.
Check: Lab3_register.csv is in your Lab 3 folder.

9Run the checker[8]

  1. In the terminal: cd Documents/420-1C2/Lab3, then python kalmia_risk_register.py Lab3_register.csv --lab3.
  2. Correct each REJECTED row in the workbook, export again and run again.
  3. When it prints RESULT: READY TO SUBMIT, save the report: python kalmia_risk_register.py Lab3_register.csv --lab3 > checker_report.txt.
Check: The last line reads RESULT: READY TO SUBMIT.

10ZIP the five files and submit them[9][10]

  1. Write the one-page memo to Nadia Roy and save it as PDF (Portable Document Format).
  2. Select the workbook, Lab3_register.csv, checker_report.txt, priority_list.csv and the memo → right-click → compress to a ZIP file named Lab3_LastName_FirstName.zip.
  3. Upload it in the Omnivox Léa drop box (Assignments → Lab 3) before Friday, November 20, 2026, 23:59 (Montréal time, EST [Eastern Standard Time], UTC [Coordinated Universal Time]−05:00).
Check: You keep the submission confirmation.

Footnotes — where your screen or version may differ

  1. Python screens are simplified drawings based on the Python 3.15.0 Windows installer (64-bit), October 2026. python.org now lists the Python install manager first: with it, type py install 3.15 in a terminal instead of using these screens. On macOS 10.15 or later the .pkg installer shows different screens. If typing python opens the Microsoft Store, install from python.org instead.
  2. The terminal prompt differs: Windows PowerShell shows PS C:\Users\name>; the macOS Terminal shows name@computer ~ %.
  3. File Explorer (Windows) and Finder (macOS) draw files differently; any folder works as long as the seven files are together.
  4. Excel for Microsoft 365 and LibreOffice Calc 26.8 show the same cells but different ribbons and menus; drop-down arrows appear only when a cell is selected.
  5. The identifiers inside the heat-map cells use the TEXTJOIN function: Excel 2019, 2021, 2024, Microsoft 365 or LibreOffice Calc. In Excel 2016 these cells show a function-name error; the counts under the matrix still work.
  6. The prioritizer page works offline in current Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari; the CSV (comma-separated values) file never leaves your computer. Title lines, empty template rows and semicolon-separated files are accepted.
  7. Dialog drawn after Excel for Microsoft 365 on Windows (November 2026). Excel for Mac: File → Save As → File Format → CSV UTF-8 (Comma delimited). French-language Excel: CSV UTF-8 (délimité par des virgules) — the checker also accepts semicolons. LibreOffice 26.8: File → Save a Copy → Text CSV (.csv) → Use Text CSV Format → character set Unicode (UTF-8). The warning about multiple sheets is worded differently in each program.
  8. Output abridged with “…”; your rows, counts and messages depend on your register. Row R-14 and its correction are an invented example.
  9. The course portal is a generic drawing, not Omnivox: Léa looks different, labels can appear in French (Travaux, Remettre) and may change after an update. If the drop box does not appear, write to the professor through MIO (the Omnivox internal messaging service) before the deadline.
  10. Windows 11: right-click → “Compress to” → “ZIP File” (older versions: Send to → Compressed (zipped) folder). macOS: right-click → “Compress”.
